assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a superconducting artificial atom strongly coupled to a single microwave photon in a resonator, giving dispersive readout, controlled coupling and the architecture on which essentially all superconducting quantum processors run. It opened a new regime of light-matter interaction on a chip and is conceptually clean, original and enormously consequential.
assessment.attribution: Blais (with Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) wrote the 2004 theory proposal; Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004 experimentally. The three-person split is natural, theory plus the two experimental groups. Girvin's contribution to the theory is not in the credited names, so the allocation is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: Strong coupling has been reproduced across many laboratories and platforms for two decades and is routine. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, so this is the natural next step and timing is good, though the committee may wish to leave some distance from 2025.
uncertainties: Whether a second superconducting-circuit prize so soon after 2025 is balanced for the Academy.
Credit for the original theory proposal beyond the named theorist (Girvin, Huang) is outside the supplied credited names.
My own proximity to this field means I should be cautious about overweighting it and defer to colleagues on relative ranking.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realisation gave the first fully controllable multi-qubit quantum processors, with the highest-fidelity gates and the benchmark against which other platforms are measured. It is foundational for quantum computing and quantum simulation.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 proposal; Blatt's group realised the gate and scaled entangled-state control. Wineland (already honoured in 2012) and Monroe are important contributors outside the supplied names, which complicates the picture. The three-person configuration is defensible but overlaps with the Cirac-Zoller entries in other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, reproduced in many laboratories and commercialised. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue given the 2012 prize covered trapped-ion control more broadly.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for measurement and manipulation of individual quantum systems may be seen as partial duplication.
Whether the prize should credit the Cirac-Zoller theory more broadly across platforms (ions, atoms) rather than ions alone.
Roles of Wineland and Monroe in the first gate demonstrations are not in the credited set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength concept and developed by Ye into clocks at the 10^-18 level, transformed time and frequency metrology and enables tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. It is a clear, controllable quantum system that opened a new precision regime.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice idea and Ye led the highest-precision realisations. The two-person configuration is a natural fit. Hall and Hansch (frequency combs, 2005) and Wineland's ion clocks are prior prizes in the neighbourhood.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by several laboratories worldwide, with a redefinition of the second under active discussion. Maturity is high and the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes.
Contributions of other early lattice-clock groups (e.g. Lemonde, Takamoto) are not in the credited names.
I defer to AMO colleagues on metrological priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators opened a whole class of topological band phases, with experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells and later three-dimensional materials. The discovery changed condensed-matter physics and fed into Majorana and topological-qubit research.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the original theory, with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposing HgTe and Molenkamp's group providing the 2007 experimental observation. The omission of Zhang and Bernevig-Hughes leaves a real attribution tension, though the supplied trio is a coherent theory plus experiment configuration. This is outside my core field and I defer to condensed-matter colleagues.
assessment.maturity: Robustly confirmed in many materials and with ARPES and transport; the field is very mature. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Credit among Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Molenkamp, and the separate role of Moore, Balents, Roy and Fu and Kane for 3D.
The relationship to the closely related candidate B004, which includes Qi-Kun Xue instead of Mele.
Outside my core expertise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction, with Shor's nine-qubit code, Steane's CSS-type codes and Kitaev's topological codes, showed that quantum information can in principle be protected, which is the conceptual basis for fault-tolerant quantum computing. Importantly, the conceptual discovery is deep and original.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane independently found the first codes in 1995-96; Kitaev introduced the surface and toric code. Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme and Aharonov-Ben-Or are important and not in the credited set, so the three-person configuration is contested.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations of below-threshold error correction in superconducting and ion platforms (2023-2025) strengthen the case, but full-scale fault-tolerant computing is still ahead. The discovery is a theory result with maturing experimental confirmation.
uncertainties: Fault-tolerant computing itself is not yet demonstrated at scale, so the prize would reward the concept rather than a technology.
Fair allocation among Shor, Steane, Kitaev, Gottesman, Calderbank, Knill and others is difficult.
The Nobel Committee for Physics tradition with respect to pure quantum information theory is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, with correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity in a tunable, clean platform. A new regime of physics, experimentally controllable and widely extended into other moire systems.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed the correlated insulator and superconductivity in 2018. Cao and the Fu, Kaxiras and Santos-Castro Neto contributions are relevant; the first-author experimentalist Yuan Cao is not in the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Observations have been reproduced by multiple groups, but the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated, so interpretation is not yet stable.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity and correlated states remains unsettled.
Sample-dependence and twist-angle disorder complicate reproducibility.
Outside my core expertise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programmable Rydberg-atom tweezer arrays enabled coherent many-body quantum simulation, with new phases and large-scale entangled states, and have become a leading platform for neutral-atom quantum computing with high-fidelity gates.
assessment.attribution: Saffman proposed Rydberg blockade quantum gates with Zoller, Jaksch and Lukin; Browaeys and Lukin demonstrated programmable arrays and quantum simulation. Bernien, Endres, Greiner, Ahn and Weiss are important contributors outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing and reproduced by many groups, though much of the work is recent. Recognition is perhaps slightly early relative to trapped ions and lattice clocks.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among many leading groups is diffuse.
Recent timing and whether the platform's breakthrough is a single discovery or a technology evolution.
Overlap with Cirac-Zoller candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum control of mechanical motion, from ground-state cooling and quantum-state preparation of nanomechanical resonators to optomechanical squeezing and entanglement, brought macroscopic objects into the quantum regime. Cleland's piezoelectric resonator coupled to a superconducting qubit and the phonon work in circuits relate to experiments I know well.
assessment.attribution: Cleland demonstrated ground-state cooling and Fock-state control of a mechanical resonator with a qubit (2010); Aspelmeyer and Kippenberg developed cavity optomechanics, with cooling and strong coupling. Many others (Schwab, Painter, Lehnert, Teufel, Regal) contributed equally; a fair three-person split is hard.
assessment.maturity: Well established and reproduced in many laboratories, although applications and a single decisive discovery remain unclear. Timing is reasonable but the case is less crisp than the higher-ranked candidates.
uncertainties: Diffuse credit among several groups and platforms.
Whether the discovery is a single conceptual advance or a family of techniques.
Potential overlap with the 2025 prize theme of macroscopic quantum behaviour in circuits.
